title: ⭐⭐ Revision: A Journey Around the World

questions.prompt: Which letter on a map stands for the direction west?
questions.explanation: West begins with the letter W, and it is the direction on the left of the map. The letter E stands for east on the right, N for north at the top and S for south at the bottom.

questions.prompt: In which country is the amphitheatre of El Jem?
questions.explanation: The amphitheatre of El Jem is a Roman monument built about 1800 years ago in Tunisia. Egypt is the country of the pyramids, France the country of the Eiffel Tower, and China the country of the Great Wall.

Throwing tomatoes at a festival is La Tomatina, a custom of Spain. Eating couscous on Friday is a Tunisian custom, touching noses to say hello is the Maori greeting of New Zealand, and wearing a blazer is a school habit and not the custom of any country.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means exactly the same as "I prefer to travel by plane"?

options.text: I prefer to travelling by plane.

questions.explanation: Prefer has two correct shapes that say the same thing: prefer to plus the bare verb, and prefer plus the verb with -ing, so I prefer travelling by plane is the twin sentence. Putting to in front of travelling joins the two shapes, the bare travel cannot follow prefer alone, and I travel by plane only tells what you do, not what you like more.

questions.prompt: Complete: "The Great Wall of China is ___ wall on Earth."
questions.explanation: Every wall on Earth makes one big group, and for the first place of a group a short adjective takes the in front and -est behind: the longest wall on Earth. The form the longer compares two walls only, longest than mixes the two tools, and most never joins a short English adjective.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Spain is ___ country in the south-west of Europe."
questions.explanation: The sentence says what Spain is, one country among many, and the word country begins with the consonant c, so the little word is a. The form an waits for a vowel, the points at a country already known, and of does not stand in front of a noun like this one.
